_derivation: Each row's label is DERIVED from crAPI's official OpenAPI spec (p0/corpus/crapi-openapi-spec.json, OWASP/crAPI). 'enforces_ownership' is true iff the endpoint defines a 403 'not allowed' response; 'leaks_cross_user' is read from whether the spec's own example payload exposes another principal's data. Independent assessment reports corroborate each (see corpus/PROVENANCE.md).

endpoints.spec_evidence: response example returns vehicle.owner {email: victim.one@example.com, number}; report_id is int32, sequential; no 403 path defined
endpoints.label: VULN

endpoints.spec_evidence: returns {carId, fullName, vehicleLocation}; only 200/404 defined; no ownership-scoped 403; vehicleId is any UUID, leaked via community posts author.vehicleid
endpoints.label: VULN

endpoints.spec_evidence: admin-only delete; 403 Forbidden defined for non-admin; reaching it as ROLE_USER is the BFLA (function-level)
endpoints.label: VULN

endpoints.spec_evidence: 403 'You are not allowed to access this resource!' IS defined -> ownership IS enforced on the order object; the violation is mass-assignment of the client-controlled 'status' (OrderStatusEnum delivered/return pending/returned) to force a refund, not cross-user BOLA
endpoints.label: VULN

endpoints.spec_evidence: recent-posts example payload exposes each author's vehicleid (UUID) + email of OTHER users (victim.one@example.com, victim.two@example.com) -> excessive data exposure that seeds the vehicle BOLA
endpoints.label: VULN

endpoints.spec_evidence: returns ONLY the authenticated user's fields (id,name,email,role,...); independent reports note this endpoint correctly ignores any id param -> 'security done right'
